title: Conserved Transcriptomic Heat Stress Response Signatures in Coral Recruits From Crosses of Thermally Distinct Broodstock.
abstract: Thermal history provenancing can guide the choice of parental broodstock for selective breeding of corals from distinct reefs and has been proposed as an intervention for enhancing climate resilience. However, the genetic and molecular mechanisms underlying resultant offspring responses to heat stress, particularly during early life stages, remain poorly understood. Here, we generated Acropora tersa larvae and recruits by crossing parental colonies from the historically warmer Martin Reef and cooler Davies Reef and assessed the effects of within- and between-reef crosses on genetic diversity using single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) genotyping and transcriptional responses to heat stress using ribonucleic acid sequencing (RNA-seq). Genome-wide SNP analyses showed that broodstock from Martin and Davies Reefs were weakly differentiated (FST = 0.008) and exhibited comparable heterozygosity, as did all larval offspring groups. Host RNA-seq analyses of surviving recruits exposed to heat stress (32°C for 36 days) revealed that the within- and between-reef offspring groups (n = 2 and 1 respectively) activated conserved stress-response pathways, with seven genotype-independent heat-responsive genes detected across all offspring groups. Differential expression and enrichment analyses showed induction of defence, protein homeostasis, intracellular transport, and metabolic processes alongside repression of growth- and signaling-related functions, consistent with the Type A General Coral Stress Response. Taken together, these findings indicate that within- and between-reef offspring generated to test thermal history provenancing exhibited broadly similar genetic diversity and weak differentiation alongside largely conserved host transcriptional responses to heat stress, including seven genotype-independent heat-responsive candidate genes.

title: Comparative ecotoxicity of aluminium-based galvanic anodes and impressed current on the Pacific oyster (Crassostrea gigas) larvae: A dose-response study.
abstract: Cathodic protection through aluminium-based galvanic anodes (Al-GACP) or impressed-current cathodic protection (ICCP) are widely used to prevent corrosion of submerged steel structures in seawater. These processes release cocktail of compounds, whose impact on the surrounding environment remains poorly documented. In this study, the effects of the metal cocktail released by Al-GACP and of by-products formed by the ICCP system were assessed in Crassostrea gigas oyster D-larvae. The ICCP released chlorination and bromination by-products, such as trihalomethanes, haloacetonitriles, and haloaldehydes. Both cathodic protection systems induced dose-dependent responses on embryonic development and larvae unable to develop normally at concentrations above thresholds of 117 to 187 μg L⁻¹ for Al-GACP, and with the slightly diluted (1.6-fold) stock solution of by-products for the ICCP produced after 4 h under non-renewed water conditions. Embryotoxicity tests further demonstrated interindividual variability in the sensitivity of C. gigas broodstock to Al-GACP, with an EC50 ranging from 63.4 to 110 μg L-1. These preliminary results highlight the need for further research on the ecological effects of chlorination byproducts (generated by the ICCP system) in ecotoxicological studies, in order to strike the right balance between decisions regarding the protection of offshore structures against corrosion and the conservation of marine wildlife.

title: Parity-selective tuning of higher-order mode nonlinearities in a doubly clamped MEMS beam resonator
abstract: Abstract Strain tuning can suppress or reverse the fundamental mode nonlinearity of microelectromechanical-system (MEMS) resonators. Extending this control to higher-order modes requires understanding its mode dependence. Here, we demonstrate a parity-selection rule for mode-selective nonlinear tuning in an initially curved, doubly clamped GaAs beam resonator. The nonlinear model shows that the curvature-induced quadratic nonlinearity depends on a modal overlap between the initial beam profile and the vibration mode shape. The overlap vanishes when these two profiles have opposite parity about the beam midpoint, whereas matching parity allows quadratic softening to compete with cubic hardening. Measurements of the first four out-of-plane bending modes under thermal strain tuning reproduce the grouping predicted for an even-parity initial profile. The first and third modes undergo hardening-to-softening transitions, whereas the second and fourth remain hardening over the measured heating-power range. Further calculations predict that an odd-parity initial profile enables such transitions in the second and fourth modes. These results provide a symmetry-based design guideline for mode-selective suppression and reversal of nonlinear frequency shifts.

title: Characterizing the molecular determinants of sliding clamp binding in Bacillus subtilis.
abstract: In bacteria, the ring-shaped sliding clamp, DnaN, is an essential component of the replication machinery. The clamp encircles the parental DNA strand during replication and binds DNA polymerases and other replication and repair proteins, helping to tether them at their site of action. These proteins interact with the clamp via short pentapeptide or hexapeptide sequences known as clamp-binding motifs (CBMs). Although conserved CBM sequences have been identified across bacterial species, most clamp binding studies have been performed in the model gram-negative bacterium Escherichia coli and less is known about clamp binding in other bacterial species. In this study, we investigate clamp binding in the model gram-positive bacterium Bacillus subtilis. We use fluorescence polarization assays to quantify binding of a range of CBM peptides to both the E. coli and B. subtilis DnaN clamps. We identify similarities in clamp binding between the two species, including similar amino acid importance within the conserved pentapeptide motif. However, our results also reveal differences in clamp binding, most notably that hexapeptide CBMs bind an order of magnitude more weakly to the B. subtilis clamp. Our results provide new insight into sliding clamp binding in bacteria and point to possible species-specific differences in this essential interaction.
journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society

title: Diverging light-responsive behaviors in genetically similar strains of Hydra vulgaris
abstract: Sensory perception drives behavior by bridging the external environment with internal states. The freshwater cnidarian Hydra vulgaris serves as a useful model for capturing these dynamics due to its structural simplicity and distinct, state-dependent behaviors. However, few studies examine behavioral differences between strains that may arise from distinct genetic backgrounds, and none have compared behaviors from closely related lines. Here, we compare the phototactic profiles of two independently derived F1 lines created by self-crossing the standard laboratory AEP line: Hydra vulgaris AEP Irvine and AEP Kiel. While satiety alters behavior in both lines, starved AEP Irvine animals display stochastic wandering rather than the robust positive phototaxis seen in the AEP Kiel strain. A biased-correlated random walk model reproduces both behaviors by modifying jump rate and head angle. Despite lacking directional phototaxis, AEP Irvine remains light-sensitive: in darkness, animals exhibit fewer jumps, greater jump distance, and longer head-angle persistence. Behavioral motif classification reveals that light exposure alters time spent in stillness and elongation, as well as a few transition probabilities. These findings highlight behavioral differences between Hydra strains derived from the same parental line, providing an opportunity to identify molecular and genetic mechanisms coupling photoreception to state-dependent directional navigation.

title: Universal Versus Selective Sampling of Umbilical Cord Gases in University-Based, Academic Community-Based, and Private Practice Settings: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Background Umbilical cord blood gas analysis provides an objective assessment of fetal metabolic status at delivery and may aid in identifying acute intrapartum hypoxic-ischemic events and newborns at risk for neurologic injury. However, there is no consensus regarding universal versus selective cord gas sampling, and professional society recommendations vary. This study aimed to evaluate differences in umbilical cord gas sampling practices, institutional protocols, and indications for sampling among obstetric providers across university-based, academic community, and private practice settings. Methods An anonymous survey was distributed to independent obstetric providers at hospitals with labor and delivery units throughout the greater Philadelphia region, including New Jersey, from September through December 2023. Eligible respondents included physicians (MD/DO) and certified nurse-midwives who independently managed deliveries. Respondents were categorized as practicing in university-based hospitals with residents, academic community hospitals with residents, or private practices without residents. The survey assessed demographics, knowledge of institutional protocols, individual practice preferences, and indications for cord gas sampling. Pairwise comparisons were performed among practice settings using Fisher's exact test for unordered categorical variables and Wilcoxon tests for ordinal variables. Results Seventy-eight providers responded, of whom 77 met inclusion criteria: 29 (37.7%) practiced in university-based settings, 33 (42.9%) in academic community settings, and 15 (19.5%) in private practice. University-based providers were more likely to report the presence of an institutional cord gas protocol (p<0.01), favor universal cord gas sampling (p<0.05), and obtain cord gases in patients requiring fetal surveillance. Reported frequency of cord gas sampling differed significantly by practice setting, with the highest frequency in university-based hospitals, followed by academic community hospitals and private practices (p<0.05). Across practice settings, providers generally agreed that fetal growth restriction <3rd percentile, Category III fetal heart rate tracings, maternal substance use, and five-minute Apgar scores <7 were indications for cord gas sampling. No significant differences were identified in awareness of protocol specifics, institutional indications for sampling, or methods of cord gas procurement. University-based providers were more likely to report preemptively setting aside a segment of umbilical cord after delivery (p<0.001). Providers across all practice settings supported delayed cord clamping. Conclusions Umbilical cord gas sampling practices and provider preferences vary significantly by practice setting, with university-based providers reporting greater use of cord gas sampling, greater awareness of institutional protocols, and stronger preference for universal sampling compared with academic community and private practice providers. Despite these differences, providers demonstrated agreement on several high-risk clinical indications for cord gas analysis. These findings highlight variability in current practice and identify areas of provider consensus that may help inform standardized criteria for selective cord gas sampling and future prospective studies comparing selective with universal sampling.

title: A multi-epitope vaccine based on AdeK, PirA, and Omp22 elicits specific antibodies binding to Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
abstract: The World Health Organization (WHO) has classified Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) as a critical-priority pathogen that requires novel antibiotics and strategies, due to its high antibiotic resistance. To combat the critical public health threat posed by CRAB, bioinformatics and immunoinformatic tools were used in this study to predict potential linear B lymphocyte (LBL), helper T lymphocyte (HTL), and cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) epitopes derived from the Acinetobacter baumannii (A. baumannii) outer membrane proteins AdeK, PirA, and outer membrane protein 22 (Omp22). Subsequently, four combined multi-epitope vaccines (MEVs) designated ABV1-ABV4 were constructed by linking selected LBL, HTL, and CTL epitopes and Pan-HLA-DR reactive epitopes (PADRE) via GGGS and AAY linkers and fusing four different adjuvants to the N-terminus of the constructs with EAAAK linkers to increase immunogenicity. Afterward, the allergenicity, antigenicity, and solubility of ABV1-ABV4 were analyzed. The two non-allergenic candidates ABV3 and ABV4 were further analyzed for physicochemical properties and immune simulation using ExPASy ProtParam and C-ImmSim. ABV4 exhibited superior antigenicity and solubility compared with ABV3, and both ABV4 and ABV3 were predicted to induce similar immune responses; therefore, ABV4 was selected for further structural characterization and subsequent expression. The 3D structure was modeled using AlphaFold 3.0 and refined with GalaxyRefine servers. After refinement, the quality of the 3D structure improved markedly, with 97.2% of the residues in the most favored regions of the Ramachandran plot and an overall Z score of -6.11. Docking scores were -274.02 kcal/mol for ABV4-TLR2 and -302.54 kcal/mol for ABV4-TLR4. MM/PBSA calculations yielded binding free energies of -53.66 kcal/mol for ABV4-TLR2 and -68.93 kcal/mol for ABV4-TLR4. The optimized ABV4 gene was synthesized, cloned and inserted into pET28a, and expressed in E. coli BL21 with a C-terminal 6 × His tag. Immunization of mice with ABV4 induced high titers of anti-ABV4 antibodies and elevated serum IFN-γ and IL-4 levels, suggesting that ABV4 may elicit both humoral and cellular immune responses in mice. Immunofluorescence assay (IFA) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) revealed that the ABV4 antibody specifically recognized CRAB extracellular proteins without cross-reactivity to E. coli, K. pneumoniae, or P. aeruginosa, confirming that ABV4 is a promising MEV vaccine candidate against CRAB with the potential to induce humoral and cellular immune responses. Overall, ABV4 is a promising vaccine candidate against CRAB, and further experimental research is required to validate the protective efficacy in mice and elucidate the underlying mechanisms.

title: Discriminative value of serum adiponectin as a potential adjunctive marker for HOMA-IR-defined insulin resistance in women with unexplained recurrent spontaneous abortion.
abstract: Insulin resistance (IR) is increasingly recognized as a modifiable contributor to unexplained recurrent spontaneous abortion (uRSA), yet its routine surrogate, the homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), requires fasting glucose and insulin measurement and therefore an overnight fast, which is inconvenient in routine reproductive-clinic workflows. HOMA-IR is itself a surrogate index rather than the gold standard for insulin sensitivity (the hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic clamp), and any downstream marker must be interpreted accordingly. Adiponectin is an insulin-sensitizing adipokine with low biological variability and limited post-prandial fluctuation. We evaluated whether serum adiponectin, measured in this study from fasting oral-glucose-tolerance-test samples, could serve as an adjunctive marker for HOMA-IR-defined IR in women with uRSA. We performed a single-centre retrospective observational study of women managed for uRSA at a tertiary maternal and child health hospital in Dongguan, southern China. All participants were of Chinese Han ethnicity. Serum total adiponectin was quantified by latex-enhanced immunoturbidimetry (Sekisui Medical Co., Tokyo, Japan; catalogue No. 17083) on a Hitachi 7180 automated analyser, with an intra-assay coefficient of variation (CV) of 3.2% and an inter-assay CV of 5.1%. Adiponectin was measured from the fasting blood sample obtained for the oral glucose tolerance test, and IR was defined as HOMA-IR ≥ 2.41. The primary analysis was conducted in the non-pregnant subgroup (n = 346), with the full cohort (n = 404, including 58 early-pregnant women) analysed secondarily. The relationship between adiponectin and HOMA-IR was assessed by Spearman correlation; adiponectin was compared between IR and non-IR groups using the Mann-Whitney U test. Discriminative performance was quantified by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with the optimal cut-off identified by the Youden index. Incremental discrimination of adiponectin beyond age and body mass index (BMI) was evaluated by nested-model AUC comparison using the DeLong test. Sensitivity analyses were conducted with alternative HOMA-IR thresholds (2.0, 2.5 and 3.0). Multivariable logistic regression was used to adjust for age, BMI and sampling status. Among 404 women (346 non-pregnant, 58 early-pregnant; all Chinese Han), 203 (50.2%) met the criterion for HOMA-IR-defined IR. Serum adiponectin was significantly lower in the IR group than in the non-IR group (median 6.40 [interquartile range 5.20-8.70] versus 8.50 [6.90-11.10] µg/mL; P < 0.001) and was inversely correlated with HOMA-IR (Spearman ρ = -0.455, 95% confidence interval [CI] - 0.529 to - 0.374; P < 0.001), with a graded decline across ascending HOMA-IR quartiles (P for trend < 0.001). In the primary non-pregnant analysis, adiponectin yielded an AUC of 0.733 (95% CI 0.680-0.786); in the full cohort the AUC was 0.711 (95% CI 0.661-0.761). Adding adiponectin to a model containing age and BMI increased the AUC from 0.759 to 0.788 (DeLong P = 0.038). In the primary non-pregnant analysis, the optimal cut-off of ≤ 6.60 µg/mL provided a sensitivity of 58.3%, a specificity of 78.7%, a positive predictive value of 72.1% and a negative predictive value of 66.7%, with a positive likelihood ratio of 2.73. Sensitivity analyses with HOMA-IR thresholds of 2.0, 2.5 and 3.0 yielded consistent AUCs (0.697-0.724). Each 1 µg/mL decrease in adiponectin was independently associated with IR (adjusted odds ratio 1.17, 95% CI 1.06-1.29; P = 0.002). In this retrospective single-centre observational study, serum adiponectin measured from fasting samples showed a consistent inverse association with HOMA-IR-defined IR and moderate, specificity-weighted discrimination in women with uRSA. Adiponectin provided modest incremental discrimination beyond age and BMI. Although insufficiently sensitive to replace fasting indices, a low adiponectin concentration may increase clinical suspicion for IR and help triage women for confirmatory fasting assessment. These findings require prospective validation in independent cohorts before adiponectin can be recommended as a clinical triage marker; the study does not demonstrate that adiponectin predicts pregnancy prognosis or that adiponectin-guided management improves reproductive outcomes.

title: A Postbiotic Mixture of Two Heat-Inactivated Lactobacilli Preserves Gut Microbiome Integrity in Pacific White Shrimp (Penaeus vannamei)
abstract: Postbiotics represent a stable, biosafe alternative to live probiotics in aquaculture. This study evaluated the effects of a postbiotic derived from heat-inactivated cultures of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus (CNCM I-3698) and Companilactobacillus pabuli (CNCM I-3699) on the intestinal microbiome of juvenile white shrimp (Penaeus vannamei). Shrimp were fed a commercial diet supplemented with the postbiotic at 0.5 kg per metric ton (kg/MT) for 30 days (n = 15 per group). Intestinal bacterial communities were profiled by 16S rRNA gene (V3–V4) amplicon sequencing. Alpha diversity, phylum-level composition (dominated by Pseudomonadota, Bacteroidota, and Bacillota), beta diversity, and Gram-positive-to-Gram-negative ratios did not differ significantly between the Control and Treatment groups, and no differentially abundant amplicon sequence variants were identified. Vibrio, the dominant genus and one that includes major shrimp pathogens, was further examined at the species level. No Vibrio species differed significantly between groups, including the most abundant assignable species, V. owensii. These results indicate that the postbiotic can be incorporated into shrimp feed without perturbing the resident intestinal microbiota. This microbiome stability supports its use as a functional feed additive in antibiotic-free shrimp aquaculture.

title: Starfish-FL: Harnessing Agentic Federated Analytics
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving multi-site clinical research, but orchestrating, monitoring, and interpreting federated analyses remain out of reach for the biostatisticians and clinicians who most need them. We present Starfish-FL, a multi-tier agent harness for cross-silo healthcare analytics built around the safety invariant that the LLM is advisory and cannot independently trigger consequential actions. Agents operate at three tiers. An Autonomous Experiment Agent orchestrates end-to-end experiments via CLI tools, an Embedded Router Agent handles adaptive aggregation, early stopping, and failure triage, and Controller Agent Hooks produce per-site summaries, outlier flags, and convergence signals. Three hybrid safety policies, SafeStop, SafeAggregate, and SafeTriage, gate every site exclusion, early stop, and recovery action behind deterministic preconditions, so LLM errors cannot cause unsafe state transitions, conditional on guard correctness. All agent features are opt-in and degrade gracefully to standard FL, and the platform provides 21 Python and R task implementations with built-in statistical diagnostics. Evaluated across four LLM providers with repeated-run confidence intervals, task selection reaches \({\sim}97\%\) accuracy with hosted models, the online SafeStop policy saves 50–70% of rounds with no accuracy loss, and safety-policy validation shows a 100% safe-action rate under injected failures, confirming that deterministic guards, not the LLM, preserve safety.
journal: ACM Transactions on Computing for Healthcare

title: Food ration affects mRNA processing, translation, proteostasis and cytoskeletal responses during heat shock in Mytilus californianus
abstract: Despite a likely role in setting stress tolerance limits, food ration has received limited attention as an ecological factor affecting the cellular stress response (CSR). To study the interactive effects of food and temperature on the proteomic heat shock response, we acclimated intertidal mussels (Mytilus californianus) to four combinations of nearshore (low) and aquaculture (high) phytoplankton levels, combined with low (20°C) and high (30°C) aerial temperatures during daytime low tides. Mussels were then exposed to an acute (6 h), aerial heat stress (33°C) and allowed to recover for 1 and 25 h in pre-exposure conditions. Proteomic changes in the gill before and after heat shock were measured using label-free liquid-chromatography-mass spectrometry. Compared with other acclimation treatments, low temperature-low food (LTLF) mussels modified more splicing factors, heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoproteins, ribosomal proteins, and translation initiation and elongation factors, suggesting systemic changes to RNA processing, selection and translation. LTLF mussels also increased chaperones of the actin- and microtubule-associated cytoskeleton and proteins that mature along the endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi secretory pathway. Simultaneously, actin stress fiber formation at focal adhesions and the extracellular matrix, along with anchoring of microtubule-associated cilia, indicate a possible system-wide mechanical breakdown of the cytoskeleton. Signaling proteins causing cytoskeletal changes varied mainly in LTLF mussels and suggest a food-dependent role for prostaglandin synthesis. Overall, the acclimation-dependent proteomic changes show how thermal conditioning and food ration together will shape the CSR of mussels during heat waves.

title: Functional interplay between retinoid X receptor and juvenile hormone analog regulates offspring production in Artemia parthenogenetica
abstract: The juvenile hormone (JH) signaling pathway is crucial for reproductive development, molting and metamorphosis in model insects. However, the molecular mechanisms of key components in the JH signaling pathway remain poorly understood in crustaceans. The aim of this study was to elucidate the function of the retinoid X receptor (RXR) gene and JH analogs (JHAs) in the reproductive development of the brine shrimp Artemia parthenogenetica. Using an ELISA kit, we detected JH-like immunoreactivity in A. parthenogenetica that peaks during stage IV of ovarian development, coinciding with maximal expression of the cytochrome P450 (CYP15) gene. The RXR homolog in A. parthenogenetica (Ar-RXR) features conserved DNA- and ligand-binding domains and shares close phylogenetic affinity with the Daphnia magna RXR homolog. Its expression profile aligns with JHA fluctuations, suggesting coordinated regulation of oogenesis. RNAi-mediated knockdown of Ar-RXR significantly suppressed RXR expression (P<0.01) and downregulated JH pathway genes (Ar-Met, Ar-Kr-h1, Ar-Vg), accompanied by abnormal cytological characteristics: concentric membranes and lipid droplet accumulation in fat body cells, reduced yolk granules in embryos and a decrease in the number of offspring. Conversely, JH III injection upregulated ovarian Ar-RXR and other JH pathway genes (except Ar-Kr-h1), yielding plump, well-arranged eggs. Co-injection of JH III and Ar-RXR dsRNA partially rescued JH pathway gene expression and reduced the number of egg abnormalities. Our findings demonstrate that a JH-like signal and Ar-RXR functionally interact to regulate reproductive development in A. parthenogenetica, providing mechanistic insights into JH signaling and advancing understanding of arthropod reproductive evolution.

title: From Bycatch to Blood Health: A Participatory Action Research on Family Empowerment through Baby Crab (Portunus pelagicus)-Based Local Food Modification to Prevent Anemia among Pregnant Women in Coastal Medan, Indonesia
abstract: Introduction: Maternal anemia remains a major public health problem in Indonesian coastal fishing communities, where economic, relational, informational, and cultural barriers compound nutritional vulnerability, despite the presence of underutilized local marine resources. Objectives: To identify the dimensions of powerlessness underlying maternal anemia among coastal pregnant women, to determine the iron, protein, calcium, and fat content of baby crab (Portunus pelagicus) porridge as a local functional food, and to evaluate the effect of a family empowerment strategy that combines baby crab-based food modification with the Information-Motivation-Behavioral Skills (IMB) model on hemoglobin concentration and anemia recovery. Methods: A Participatory Action Research (PAR) design was employed through five cyclical stages (Reconnaissance, Planning, Action, Observation, Reflection) in Kecamatan Medan Belawan, Indonesia. Fifty-five pregnant women with anemia (Hb <11 g/dL) received 200 g of baby crab porridge daily for 40 days combined with family-centered nutrition counseling guided by the Information-Motivation-Behavioral Skills (IMB) model; 48 completed the protocol. Sixty-four additional informants were purposively selected for qualitative interviews and focus groups, with findings systematically integrated into the quantitative evaluation. Results: A 200 g serving of 30% baby crab porridge provided 8.9 mg iron, 7.61% protein, 120.4 mg calcium, and 0.38% fat. The Reconnaissance stage identified four interlocking dimensions of powerlessness (economic, relational, informational, and cultural). Hemoglobin increased significantly across the intervention (Day 0→40: +2.08 g/dL; p<0.001; Cohen's d=2.15), with 77.1% of participants (37/48) reaching Hb ≥11 g/dL by Day 40. Conclusions: A family-centered empowerment strategy that combines baby crab, a novel, locally sourced, iron-rich coastal food, with the IMB model constitutes a theoretically grounded and highly replicable approach for accelerating anemia recovery among pregnant women in resource-limited coastal communities.

title: Beyond Alignment: Whitening Geometry, Profile Synthesis, and Heterogeneous Ensembles for Cross-Environment WiFi Action Recognition
abstract: Cross-environment deployment is the central obstacle to practical WiFi sensing: a pipeline reaching 0.89+ top-1 in its training environments collapses to 0.408 under Leave-One-Domain-Out (LODO) evaluation with only K-shot labels. A ceiling analysis shows the collapse is not an alignment problem: the action signal is strong across seen environments (about 0.89 K10), environment identity is decodable from the encoder (0.965), and the failure concentrates in the encoder's extrapolation to the novel environment. A pre-registered falsification chain confirms that "align the domains" methods--training-time alignment, readout-level prototype alignment, adversarial confusion, and covariance/subspace alignment (CORAL -3.8pp, subspace -8.3pp)--degrade performance, and that source-domain statistics anti-correlate with cross-environment contribution. The effective levers lie elsewhere; we combine them into Dec-H: (i) closed-form source within-class whitening, provably re-geometrizing the readout's L2 regularization (+8.6pp, zero cost); (ii) profile-mixing augmentation (+1.0pp); (iii) few-shot adaptation with alternating whitening refit (+1.5pp; fixed preconditioners are 20/20 negative); (iv) heterogeneous decision ensembles (+1.7pp); homogeneous scaling and source-weighted stacking are saturated or harmful. Dec-H reaches 0.560 K10 (0.812 K40), +15.2pp over the baseline, consistent across all four environments and seeds; all thirteen configurations were pre-registered with frozen criteria.

title: Leveraging Local English Communication Skills as a Catalyst for Sustainable Tourism Growth: A Case Study of Sekotong, Lombok
abstract: The rapid growth of international marine tourism in Sekotong, West Lombok, demands competent human resources capable of bridging cross-cultural communication and promoting environmental stewardship. This study investigates the existing English communication competence of the local coastal community in Sekotong, analyzes how communication barriers affect marine conservation and cultural preservation, and formulates a contextual English for Tourism and Conservation (ETC) learning model. Employing a qualitative descriptive approach with an intrinsic case study design, data were collected over three to four months in Batu Putih Village, Gili Asahan, and Gili Gede through semi-structured interviews with fifteen purposively selected key informants—local tour guides, Pokdarwis members, tourism SME operators, and village officials—participatory observation, and analysis of twenty-two visual artifacts drawn from the linguistic landscape. Data were analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, comprising data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. Trustworthiness was ensured through source and method triangulation, member checking, and thick description, while research ethics were observed through informed consent, anonymity, and cultural sensitivity toward Sasak community norms. The findings reveal a stark dichotomy between transactional and interactional competence. While local stakeholders demonstrate basic transactional proficiency at the CEFR A1 level—relying on telegraphic speech, isolated vocabulary, and non-verbal gestures for routine commercial exchanges—they experience severe deficits in interactional competence, often resorting to strategic avoidance, manifesting as silent withdrawal, during complex inquiries. Furthermore, grammatical distortions in public signage, such as "No Step Corals," undermine the institutional authority of local conservation groups. These linguistic barriers directly compromise coral reef protection, Sasak cultural integrity, and maritime safety, while confining locals to low-margin labor as external agencies dominate high-value guided tours. Treating English as vital soft infrastructure, this study proposes an applied, task-based ETC framework comprising three modules: Practical Marine Hospitality, Environmental Stewardship Discourse, and Sasak Cultural Narratives, designed to empower local hosts as autonomous custodians of sustainable tourism. The study concludes that English communication competence is a precondition for local empowerment rather than a mere service skill, and recommends the piloting of the ETC model within community empowerment programs. Keywords: English for Tourism and Conservation; sustainable tourism; soft infrastructure; local empowerment; Sekotong
